implementation_notes: SUPERSEDED (this note described the original implementation and is retained for the record): toOllamaFilteredMessages (src/lib/token-view.ts) is a hand-kept, line-by-line mirror of server/ollama-client.ts's private toOllamaMessages (~245-301) — the only legal way to reuse its filtering rules given architecture.md's server/src boundary. This is the sole source for both AC-UX-5's outgoing-message rendering and AC-UX-6/AC-TOK-5's reconciliation slice; requestJsonPreview (buildOpenAIRequestBody/toOpenAIMessages) is never touched by either path. || CURRENT STATE: the mirror was eliminated, not patched. A Stage-1 review proved it diverged from the server in 3 of 5 congruence cases (a `system` step after a pending tool_call failed to flush; both the `&& step.toolCall` and `&& step.toolResult` payload guards were dropped), violating AC-TOK-5's 'filtered exactly as toOllamaMessages filters them'. Remediation extracted the single implementation into shared/ollama-format.ts over the pre-existing FormatStep structural interface (reused unmodified; `git diff shared/openai-format.ts` is empty). server/ollama-client.ts imports it and its two local copies (~78 lines) were deleted; src/lib/token-view.ts's toOllamaFilteredMessages now delegates to the same function. Equivalence with the deleted S1 code was proven mechanically: diffing the deleted body against the shared body yields exactly 2 changed lines, both type annotations. Guarded by tests/integration/ollama-format-congruence.test.ts, which drives BOTH real production entry points (buildOllamaChatBody and toOllamaFilteredMessages) over the 5-case table including the three previously-divergent shapes.

AC-TOK-5's 'steps[0..i)' slice and AC-UX-6's tool-call-turn gate are two distinct, separately-tested functions: findLastUsageStep (locates the last usage-bearing assistant step) and turnHasToolCall (scoped to the turn producing that step — walks back only to the nearest preceding user step, not the whole conversation). This scoping matters: a tool-call turn earlier in a long-running conversation must not permanently disable reconciliation for every later, tool-free turn — pinned by a dedicated test.

Model-staleness discipline (carried forward from S3's invariant-computed-boundary-model-key): useTokenizedMessages/useReconciliation key their tokenize cache on (message contents, cacheKeySuffix), with RequestPreviewExtras passing the conversation's model name as cacheKeySuffix to BOTH call sites. Without this, switching models while the request-preview dialog is open would keep serving token counts computed under the OLD model against content that looks unchanged (same class of bug S3 fixed in useTokenBoundaries, here reintroduced deliberately as a discipline to follow, not a bug to discover).

No new server round trip: the verbatim /api/show template is fetched via the PRE-EXISTING src/lib/ollama.ts fetchModelMeta() (POST /models/show, non-verbose) — the same endpoint the model-metadata dialog already uses via handleOpenModelMeta. RequestPreviewExtras calls it independently (its own loading/error state), so the two UI surfaces never share or race on chat-workspace.tsx's modelMeta/modelMetaLoading/modelMetaError state.

AC-STRUCT-3 budget: all filtering/tokenization/reconciliation-arithmetic lives in src/lib/token-view.ts; all new JSX lives in a new src/components/request-preview-extras.tsx file (mirroring S2's token-view-step-content.tsx precedent). chat-workspace.tsx's own net addition is a 3-line previewModel memo extraction (which also removed a duplicate inline lookup from requestJsonPreview), a 1-line import, a 2-line JsonPreviewDialog extra-prop addition, and an 8-line call-site wiring block — roughly 20 lines against 32 lines of headroom, landing the epic total at 48 of the 60-line budget.

During implementation, the first port of toOllamaFilteredMessages' tool_result branch omitted the pending-tool-call flush the real toOllamaMessages performs before pushing the tool message (a synthetic empty-content assistant message would have been silently missing). Caught by this story's own tests (tests/unit/token-view-reconciliation.test.ts's tool_call/tool_result fixture tests) before any other code depended on it — fixed in the same pass, now pinned by two dedicated tests asserting the exact message shape, not just message count.

AC-TOK-5's live-gated test (tests/integration/reconciliation-live.test.ts) builds its comparison request via server/ollama-client.ts's exported buildOllamaChatBody (the real toOllamaMessages) rather than hand-rolling a request body, so the prompt_eval_count oracle it compares against reflects exactly what production sends. It imports src/lib/token-view.ts's toOllamaFilteredMessages via a relative path (no @/ alias is configured for vitest.server.config.ts's node environment) — safe because the only value-level import that module pulls in is React (never invoked, since only its non-hook exports are used here), and its ConversationStep type import is erased at compile time.

retrospective.surprised_by: React 19 (installed in this repo) removed the global ambient `JSX` namespace, so `extra?: JSX.Element` on JsonPreviewDialog's props failed to typecheck (`Cannot find namespace 'JSX'`) even though the surrounding codebase never needed an explicit React type import before. Fixed by importing `type ReactNode` from "react" instead. Worth knowing before reaching for `JSX.Element` in any React-19 TypeScript codebase.
